card.title: Calculation of empirical and molecular formula from % composition (solving related numerical problems)

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Percentage composition = element mass ÷ molar mass × 100, always summing to 100: H₂SO₄ (2.04/32.65/65.31), urea N 46.67% (the bag proved), NH₄NO₃ N 35%, CaCO₃ Ca 40%. Backward: % → grams → moles → ratio → empirical (CH₂O); with M_r (often 2×VD): n = M_r/E_r → molecular (C₆H₁₂O₆; M_r 90 → C₃H₆O₃). Combustion analysis gives %C (×12/44) and %H (×2/18), O by difference.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
%E = (mass of E per mole ÷ M_r) × 100
M_r = Σ A_r
M_r = 2 × vapour density (H₂ = 2)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Mass % and mole % differ — convert with A_r before comparing.  ·  O-by-difference assumes only C, H, O present; N/S need separate estimation.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: %E = (mass of E per mole ÷ M_r) × 100; Σ%E = 100.  ·  Urea CO(NH₂)₂, M_r 60: %N = 28/60×100 = 46.67% — the "46-0-0" bag derived.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: '46-0-0' bag verified: 28/60 = 46.67% N.  ·  Limestone audit: 40% Ca expected; less means impurity.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: empirical/molecular formula from % composition (within Stoichiometry).  ·  Out of scope: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: **Scope.** Calculation of empirical and molecular formula from % composition — Stoichiometry, Chemistry (class-11-notes).  ·  **Tested.** define it · list: empirical formula, molecular formula · one worked example · one misconception each.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Combustion factors: C from CO₂ (×12/44); H from H₂O (×2/18); O by difference.  ·  n = M_r/E_r — needs measured M_r (VD×2, mass spec); never assumed.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: SHORT (2 marks): Give the % composition formula and the sum rule.  ·  SHORT (3 marks): Prove urea is 46.67% nitrogen.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Empirical gives ratio, never identity (CH₂O ×n family: glucose, formaldehyde, lactic acid).  ·  Vapour density needs the H₂ = 2 scale stated; M_r = 2×VD.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: %E = (mass of E per mole ÷ M_r) × 100; bars sum to 100.  ·  Urea N 46.67%; combustion factors 12/44 (C), 2/18 (H), O by difference.  ·  Empirical from %; molecular = n × empirical via M_r (often 2×VD).  ·  Combustion analysis: %C (×12/44), %H (×2/18), O by difference.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: M_r = 2 × vapour density (H₂ = 2 scale).

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: SHORT (3 marks): Derive CH₂O from 40% C, 6.7% H, 53.3% O data.  ·  SHORT (2 marks): How is M_r obtained from vapour density?  ·  SHORT (3 marks): From 8.8 g CO₂ + 3.6 g H₂O out of 4.4 g sample, find %C and %H.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Lactic acid shares glucose's ratio (CH₂O) — ratio is not identity.  ·  H₂SO₄ shares: 2.04% H, 32.65% S, 65.31% O (sum 100).

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: # Calculation of empirical and molecular formula from % composition (solving related numerical problems) ## 1. Topic Introduction A compound's identity is locked in its **molecular formula** — the actual number of each atom in one molecule. But elemental analysis only gives **percentage composition** — the mass % of each element.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Conceptual Understanding ### What empirical formula is The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element in a compound. It is the formula reduced to lowest terms (like a fraction). CH₂O is the empirical formula of glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆), formaldehyde (CH₂O), and lactic acid (C₃H₆O₃) — same ratio, different molecules.…  ·  ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Explanation | Importance | |------|-------------------|-------------|-------------| | Empirical formula | Simplest whole-number atom ratio in a compound | From % data: % → g → mol → ratio (÷ smallest) | First step in formula identification | | Molecular formula | Actual atom numbers in one molecule | Empirical × n; n =…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: n = M_r / E_r (empirical → molecular)  ·  %C = mass CO₂ × 12/44 × 100 / mass sample  ·  %H = mass H₂O × 2/18 × 100 / mass sample

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: %O = 100 − (%C + %H + %N + %S + ...)  ·  % yield = (actual / theoretical) × 100  ·  Vapour density: M_r = 2×VD (H₂=2); quality audit uses forward route.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Balance precision (±0.1 mg) decides analysis quality; ±0.001 g on 0.1 g sample = ±1%.  ·  Ionic salts (NaCl) stop at empirical — no molecular formula for giant lattice.  ·  % yield >100% indicates impure product or incomplete drying, not excess product.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: NH₄NO₃ N% = 35% — poorer N per kg than urea's 46.67%.  ·  LONG (5 marks): Explain percentage composition with the H₂SO₄ and urea computations.  ·  LONG (5 marks): Derive empirical and molecular formulae from analysis data with the combustion-analysis route.
